metadata.document_title: RHOBS Next and Synthetic Monitoring E2E Test Plan
metadata.purpose: Establish automated end-to-end smoke tests for RHOBS Next components (rhobs-synthetics-api, rhobs-synthetics-agent, route-monitor-operator) using the osde2e testing framework. Verify metrics, logs, and synthetic monitoring probes work correctly after each code change.
metadata.target_audience: SRE Engineers, QE Team, Platform Engineers, New Engineers Onboarding to RHOBS
learning_objectives: Understand the complete RHOBS Next synthetic monitoring architecture
Learn how route-monitor-operator creates and manages synthetic probes
Master the probe lifecycle from creation to execution to metrics collection
Understand multi-tenant probe management via rhobs-synthetics-api
Learn how rhobs-synthetics-agent reconciles probes into Kubernetes resources
Understand metrics forwarding from blackbox-exporter to Prometheus/Thanos
Learn osde2e framework for automated E2E testing in stage environments

required_access.name: OpenShift cluster admin
required_access.how_to_get: Request via service desk or use ROSA CLI

synthetic_monitoring.title: Synthetic Monitoring
synthetic_monitoring.description: Synthetic monitoring proactively tests system availability by simulating user interactions from external vantage points. Unlike passive monitoring which waits for real users to report issues, synthetic probes continuously execute predefined checks (HTTP requests, API calls, etc.) and measure response time, availability, and correctness.
synthetic_monitoring.why_it_matters: Synthetic monitoring detects issues before customers do, provides SLA validation, establishes performance baselines, and enables testing from multiple geographic regions. For RHOBS, it ensures cluster routes remain accessible and responsive.

route_monitor_operator.title: Route Monitor Operator (RMO)
route_monitor_operator.description: An OpenShift operator that watches for RouteMonitor and ClusterUrlMonitor custom resources and automatically configures synthetic probes. For standard clusters, it creates ServiceMonitor resources that configure Prometheus to scrape blackbox-exporter. For HyperShift HostedControlPlanes, it creates probe definitions in the RHOBS Synthetics API.
route_monitor_operator.why_it_matters: RMO automates probe creation, eliminating manual configuration. It bridges the gap between cluster routes (what needs monitoring) and monitoring infrastructure (how to monitor it), enabling declarative monitoring-as-code.

rhobs_synthetics_api.title: RHOBS Synthetics API
rhobs_synthetics_api.description: A multi-tenant central repository for probe configurations, built on Observatorium. It provides RESTful endpoints for creating, listing, updating, and deleting probe definitions. Each probe belongs to a tenant and includes target URL, labels, and execution status. The API enforces authentication via OIDC tokens and authorization via tenant-based access control.
rhobs_synthetics_api.why_it_matters: The API decouples probe definition (what to monitor) from probe execution (where monitoring happens). Multiple agents can subscribe to the same API, enabling centralized configuration with distributed execution. This is critical for HyperShift where management clusters run agents to monitor spoke cluster routes.

rhobs_synthetics_agent.title: RHOBS Synthetics Agent
rhobs_synthetics_agent.description: A Kubernetes controller that reconciles probe definitions from the RHOBS Synthetics API into Kubernetes resources. It polls one or more API endpoints periodically, validates probe URLs via HTTP HEAD requests, creates Probe custom resources, manages blackbox-exporter deployments, and updates probe status back to the API (pending → active → running).
rhobs_synthetics_agent.why_it_matters: The agent is the execution engine that transforms probe definitions into running checks. It handles probe lifecycle, URL validation (prevents creating probes for broken endpoints), deduplication (when same probe appears in multiple APIs), and status feedback (critical for monitoring the monitoring system).

probe_custom_resource.title: Probe Custom Resource
probe_custom_resource.description: A Kubernetes Custom Resource Definition (CRD) representing a single synthetic probe check. It specifies the target URL, HTTP method, expected status code, timeout, interval, and labels. The blackbox-exporter operator watches for Probe resources and configures blackbox-exporter to execute the checks.
probe_custom_resource.why_it_matters: Probe CRs provide a declarative, Kubernetes-native way to define monitoring checks. They integrate with GitOps workflows, support kubectl operations, and enable status tracking via .status subresource. This makes probes observable, auditable, and version-controlled.

blackbox_exporter.title: Blackbox Exporter
blackbox_exporter.description: A Prometheus exporter that executes probes (HTTP, TCP, DNS, ICMP) and exports metrics about probe results. It receives probe configurations, executes checks at specified intervals, and exposes metrics like probe_success (0/1), probe_duration_seconds, and probe_http_status_code. Prometheus scrapes these metrics for alerting and dashboarding.
blackbox_exporter.why_it_matters: Blackbox-exporter is the actual probe execution engine. It handles HTTP redirects, SSL verification, timeout handling, and various HTTP methods. Its metrics enable alerting on probe failures and tracking performance trends over time.

hostedcontrolplane.title: HyperShift HostedControlPlane
hostedcontrolplane.description: HyperShift's HostedControlPlane resource represents an OpenShift control plane running as pods in a management cluster, separate from the data plane (worker nodes). Each HostedControlPlane has an API endpoint URL that needs monitoring. RMO watches for HostedControlPlane resources and automatically creates RHOBS API probe definitions for the cluster's API endpoint.
hostedcontrolplane.why_it_matters: HyperShift enables dense multi-tenancy by running many control planes on shared infrastructure. Monitoring HostedControlPlane API endpoints via RHOBS ensures cluster availability from external vantage points, critical for detecting network partitions or control plane failures.

osde2e_framework.title: OSDe2e Testing Framework
osde2e_framework.description: OpenShift Dedicated's end-to-end testing framework. It provides utilities for creating clusters in stage environments, installing operators, running test suites, collecting logs, and reporting results to Prow/CI. Tests are written in Go using ginkgo/gomega BDD style and execute in CI pipelines after code merges.
osde2e_framework.why_it_matters: osde2e automates the full test lifecycle: provision cluster → install operators → run tests → collect results → cleanup. This enables continuous validation of RHOBS Next components with every code change, catching regressions early before they reach production.

prometheus_servicemonitor.title: Prometheus ServiceMonitor
prometheus_servicemonitor.description: A Custom Resource that declaratively configures Prometheus to scrape metrics from Kubernetes services. It specifies the service selector, port, path, interval, and scrape timeout. The Prometheus Operator watches for ServiceMonitor resources and updates Prometheus configuration dynamically without restarts.
prometheus_servicemonitor.why_it_matters: ServiceMonitors enable declarative monitoring configuration. RMO creates ServiceMonitors to tell Prometheus where to scrape blackbox-exporter metrics. This automates the 'monitoring the monitoring' setup.

metrics_forwarding.title: Metrics Forwarding to RHOBS
metrics_forwarding.description: The process of sending cluster metrics from local Prometheus to centralized RHOBS (Regional Hub for Observability). Prometheus is configured with remote_write rules that send time-series data to Thanos receivers. Each metric includes tenant labels for multi-tenancy isolation.
metrics_forwarding.why_it_matters: Centralized metrics enable cross-cluster querying, long-term retention (local Prometheus retains 2-7 days), and unified dashboards. RHOBS provides observability-as-a-service for all OpenShift Dedicated and ROSA clusters.

test_execution.objective: Verify that the Route Monitor Operator is correctly installed, running, and healthy in the OpenShift cluster before proceeding with probe creation tests.
prerequisites: OpenShift CLI (oc) installed and configured
Cluster admin access or permissions to view openshift-route-monitor-operator namespace
Route Monitor Operator installed via OLM or manual deployment

steps.title: Verify Route Monitor Operator namespace exists
steps.learning_note:
Operators in OpenShift are typically deployed in dedicated namespaces for isolation and security. The route (An OpenShift resource that exposes a service at a hostname for external access via the router) [learn more](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/routes/route-configuration.html) Monitor Operator uses the openshift-route-monitor-operator namespace by convention. Verifying the namespace exists confirms the operator installation process started successfully.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): namespaces "openshift-route-monitor-operator" not found
common_errors.cause: Route Monitor Operator not installed or installed in different namespace
common_errors.solution: Verify operator installation. Try: oc get namespaces | grep route-monitor to find the actual namespace

steps.title: Check Route Monitor Operator deployment
steps.learning_note:
A deployment (A Kubernetes resource that manages a replicated set of Pods and provides declarative updates) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/) is a Kubernetes resource that manages ReplicaSets and Pods, ensuring the specified number of pod replicas are running. The READY column shows current/desired replicas (should be 1/1). The UP-TO-DATE column indicates pods running the latest pod template. The AVAILABLE column shows pods passing readiness checks and able to serve traffic.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output:
NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE
route-monitor-operator 1/1 1 1 5d

common_errors.cause: Operator pod is not ready - could be image pull errors, crash loops, or failing health checks
common_errors.solution: Check pod status: oc get pods -n openshift-route-monitor-operator and inspect logs: oc logs deployment/route-monitor-operator -n openshift-route-monitor-operator

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): deployments.apps "route-monitor-operator" not found
common_errors.cause: Operator may use different deployment name or be deployed via StatefulSet/DaemonSet
common_errors.solution: List all deployments in namespace: oc get deployments -n openshift-route-monitor-operator

steps.title: Verify operator pod is running
steps.learning_note:
Pods are the smallest deployable units in Kubernetes, containing one or more containers. The READY column shows ready/total containers (1/1 means the single container is ready). STATUS indicates pod (The smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes - a group of one or more containers with shared storage and network) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/) phase (Running is expected). RESTARTS shows crash count - 0 is ideal, higher numbers warrant investigation.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output:
NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE
route-monitor-operator-7d8f9c5b6d-xk2mp 1/1 Running 0 5d

common_errors.cause: Cannot pull operator container image - invalid image reference, authentication failure, or network issue
common_errors.solution: Describe pod for events: oc describe pod -n openshift-route-monitor-operator <pod-name>

common_errors.cause: Operator container starts then crashes repeatedly - usually configuration error or missing permissions
common_errors.solution: Check logs: oc logs -n openshift-route-monitor-operator <pod-name> --previous (use --previous to see logs from crashed container)

common_errors.cause: Container running but failing readiness probe - operator may be starting up or experiencing errors
common_errors.solution: Wait 30 seconds and check again. If persists, check logs for readiness endpoint errors

steps.title: Inspect operator logs for activity
steps.learning_note:
Operator (A Kubernetes controller that extends the API to create, configure, and manage complex stateful applications using custom resources) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/operator/) logs provide real-time insight into the controller's operation. Healthy operators log reconciliation events, resource creation/updates, and status changes. Error logs indicate permission issues, API failures, or configuration problems. The --tail=50 flag limits output to last 50 lines for readability.

**Debugging tip:** Operator logs follow a pattern: watch events (resource created/updated/deleted), reconciliation start, validation, child resource creation, reconciliation success/failure. Understanding this pattern helps you quickly identify where reconciliation failed.
steps.expected_output:
2026-02-18T10:15:23Z INFO controller-runtime.manager starting metrics server
2026-02-18T10:15:23Z INFO setup starting manager
2026-02-18T10:15:24Z INFO controller.routemonitor Starting EventSource
2026-02-18T10:15:24Z INFO controller.routemonitor Starting Controller
2026-02-18T10:15:24Z INFO controller.routemonitor Starting workers

common_errors.error: ERROR unable to create controller: failed to get API group resources
common_errors.cause: Operator lacks RBAC permissions to watch required resources or CRDs not installed
common_errors.solution: Verify CRDs exist: oc get crd | grep routemonitor. Check operator ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding

common_errors.cause: ServiceAccount lacks permissions to create/update resources
common_errors.solution: Check operator ServiceAccount and associated RBAC: oc get clusterrolebinding | grep route-monitor

steps.title: Verify RouteMonitor CRD is installed
steps.learning_note:
Custom Resource (A Kubernetes API extension that allows you to define custom object types beyond the built-in resources like Pods and Services) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/custom-resources/) Definitions (CRDs extend the Kubernetes API with new resource types. The RouteMonitor CRD defines the schema for RouteMonitor resources. The CRD must exist before creating RouteMonitor instances. The ESTABLISHED column should show True, indicating the CRD is registered and ready for use.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

common_errors.cause: RouteMonitor CRD not installed - operator installation incomplete
common_errors.solution: Reinstall operator or manually apply CRD from operator repository: oc apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/route-monitor-operator/main/config/crd/bases/monitoring.openshift.io_routemonitors.yaml

steps.title: Verify RouteMonitor was created
steps.learning_note:
This command lists all RouteMonitor (A custom resource that declares a route should be monitored with synthetic probes) [learn more](https://github.com/openshift/route-monitor-operator) Custom Resources across all namespaces. Even if no RouteMonitors exist yet, the command succeeding confirms the CRD is properly registered and the API server recognizes the resource type. The -A flag searches all namespaces (equivalent to --all-namespaces).

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output:
No resources found
(OR if existing monitors present NAMESPACE NAME AGE
openshift-console console-monitor 5d

common_errors.error: error: the server doesn't have a resource type "routemonitors"
common_errors.cause: CRD not installed or API server hasn't registered it yet
common_errors.solution: Wait 10 seconds for API server to update, then retry. If persists, check CRD installation in previous step

success_criteria: Namespace openshift-route-monitor-operator exists with STATUS Active
Deployment route-monitor-operator shows READY 1/1
Operator pod STATUS is Running with READY 1/1
Operator logs show controller started without errors
RouteMonitor CRD exists and is established
Command 'oc get routemonitors -A' succeeds (even if no resources found)
validation.what_success_looks_like: All verification commands complete without errors. The operator deployment shows 1/1 ready replicas, the pod is running with 0 restarts, logs indicate successful controller startup, and the RouteMonitor CRD is registered. This confirms RMO is healthy and ready to reconcile RouteMonitor resources.
validation.what_failure_looks_like: Commands return NotFound errors, deployment shows 0/1 replicas, pod is in CrashLoopBackOff, logs contain permission errors or API failures, or CRD is missing. These indicate incomplete installation or configuration issues requiring remediation before proceeding.

common_issues.issue: Operator pod stuck in Pending state
common_issues.symptoms: Pod STATUS shows Pending for > 2 minutes
possible_causes: Node selector or affinity rules preventing scheduling
Pod security policies blocking pod creation
diagnostic_steps: oc describe pod -n openshift-route-monitor-operator <pod-name>
Look for Events section showing scheduling failures
Check node resources: oc describe nodes | grep -A 5 'Allocated resources'
solutions: Scale cluster to add worker nodes
Reduce operator resource requests in deployment
Remove node selector constraints
Update pod security policies

common_issues.symptoms: Pod RESTARTS count increasing, STATUS shows CrashLoopBackOff
diagnostic_steps: oc logs -n openshift-route-monitor-operator <pod-name> --previous
oc describe deployment route-monitor-operator -n openshift-route-monitor-operator
oc get clusterrole,clusterrolebinding | grep route-monitor
solutions: Review operator logs for specific error messages
Verify all required CRDs installed: oc get crd | grep monitoring.openshift.io
Check RBAC configuration matches operator requirements
Validate ConfigMap if operator uses one

common_issues.issue: CRD installed but oc get routemonitors fails
common_issues.symptoms: CRD exists but API server doesn't recognize resource type
possible_causes: API server hasn't refreshed resource cache
CRD version mismatch with API server
diagnostic_steps: oc get crd routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io -o yaml | grep -A 10 status
Check CRD conditions for Established=True
oc api-resources | grep routemonitor
solutions: Wait 30-60 seconds for API server cache refresh
Delete and reinstall CRD if validation errors present
Ensure CRD apiVersion matches cluster API server version

test_execution.objective: Create a RouteMonitor Custom Resource targeting a cluster route, verify the operator creates corresponding ServiceMonitor and configures Prometheus to scrape probe metrics.
prerequisites: Route Monitor Operator healthy and running (test_verify_route_monitor_deployment passed)
Access to create resources in test namespace
Existing OpenShift route to monitor (e.g., console route)
Permissions to view ServiceMonitors in openshift-route-monitor-operator namespace

steps.title: Create test namespace for RouteMonitor
steps.learning_note: Isolating test resources in a dedicated namespace (A Kubernetes mechanism for isolating groups of resources within a single cluster) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces/) enables easy cleanup and prevents pollution of production namespaces. Namespaces provide scope for names, RBAC policies, and resource quotas. Using a consistent naming convention (e.g., rhobs-test-* helps identify test resources.

common_errors.error: Error from server (AlreadyExists): namespaces "rhobs-test-routemonitor" already exists
common_errors.cause: Namespace exists from previous test run that wasn't cleaned up
common_errors.solution: Either delete existing namespace: oc delete namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor, or use the existing namespace

common_errors.error: Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces is forbidden
common_errors.cause: Insufficient permissions to create namespaces
common_errors.solution: Request cluster-admin access or use existing namespace where you have admin permissions

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note:
Routes expose services externally via hostname. The OpenShift console route is ideal for testing because it's always present and should return HTTP 200. The HOST column shows the URL to monitor. We'll use this in the RouteMonitor spec.route.url field.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output:
NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD
console console-openshift-console.apps.cluster.example.com console https reencrypt/Redirect None

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): routes.route.openshift.io "console" not found
common_errors.cause: Console route missing or using different name
common_errors.solution: List all routes in namespace: oc get routes -n openshift-console, pick any accessible route

steps.title: Create RouteMonitor YAML manifest
steps.learning_note: RouteMonitor is a Custom Resource (CR that extends Kubernetes API. The spec.route.url field specifies the target URL to probe. The spec.route.name and spec.route.namespace fields reference the Route object to monitor. Labels help organize and query RouteMonitors. This declarative manifest defines desired state; the operator makes it reality.
steps.command:
cat > /tmp/routemonitor.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: RouteMonitor
metadata:
 name: console-route-monitor
 namespace: rhobs-test-routemonitor
 labels:
 app: test-probe
 environment: test
spec:
 route:
 name: console
 namespace: openshift-console
EOF
cat /tmp/routemonitor.yaml
steps.expected_output:
apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: RouteMonitor
metadata:
 name: console-route-monitor
 namespace: rhobs-test-routemonitor
 labels:
 app: test-probe
 environment: test
spec:
 route:
 name: console
 namespace: openshift-console

common_errors.cause: /tmp directory has restricted permissions
common_errors.solution: Use writable directory: ~/routemonitor.yaml or $PWD/routemonitor.yaml

steps.title: Apply RouteMonitor custom resource
steps.learning_note:
The 'oc apply' command creates or updates resources declaratively. It sends the YAML to the Kubernetes API server, which validates the schema against the RouteMonitor CRD (Custom Resource Definition - the schema that defines a new custom resource type in Kubernetes) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/), then stores it in etcd. The API server then triggers watches, notifying the RMO controller that a new RouteMonitor exists. The operator reconciliation loop begins immediately.

**What happens internally:** When you run `oc apply`, the command sends the YAML to the Kubernetes API server, which validates the schema against the CRD, stores it in etcd, and triggers any controllers watching this resource type. The operator's controller immediately sees this new object and begins reconciliation.

common_errors.error: error: unable to recognize "/tmp/routemonitor.yaml": no matches for kind "RouteMonitor" in version "monitoring.openshift.io/v1alpha1"
common_errors.cause: RouteMonitor CRD not installed or wrong apiVersion
common_errors.solution: Verify CRD exists: oc get crd routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io. Check operator installation.

common_errors.error: The RouteMonitor "console-route-monitor" is invalid: spec.route.name: Required value
common_errors.cause: Required field missing in YAML spec
common_errors.solution: Ensure spec.route.name and spec.route.namespace fields are present and not empty

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note:
Listing the RouteMonitor confirms it was stored in the cluster's API server. The AGE column shows time since creation. At this point the resource exists but reconciliation (The control loop process where a controller compares desired state (spec) with actual state and takes actions to converge them) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/controller/) may not be complete. The operator watches for new RouteMonitors and queues them for processing.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io "console-route-monitor" not found
common_errors.cause: Apply command failed silently or resource created in wrong namespace
common_errors.solution: Check previous command output for errors. Try: oc get routemonitors -A | grep console

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note:
The .status subresource contains runtime state managed by the operator. The status.conditions array shows reconciliation progress. Look for conditions like 'Ready=True' or 'ServiceMonitorCreated=True'. If empty, the operator hasn't reconciled yet. The -o yaml flag outputs full resource including status.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

status:

 - lastTransitionTime: "2026-02-18T10:30:15Z"

 reason: ServiceMonitorCreated

common_errors.cause: Operator hasn't reconciled RouteMonitor yet, or reconciliation failed
common_errors.solution: Wait 30 seconds then retry. Check operator logs: oc logs deployment/route-monitor-operator -n openshift-route-monitor-operator

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note:
Kubernetes operators work asynchronously. The reconciliation loop typically completes within seconds but can take longer under load. Watching the resource shows real-time updates to status. Press Ctrl+C to stop watching once status shows Ready=True.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

NAME AGE
console-route-monitor 10s
(watch mode - wait for status updates, press Ctrl+C when ready)

steps.title: Verify ServiceMonitor creation
steps.learning_note:
RouteMonitor operator creates a ServiceMonitor (A Prometheus Operator resource that declares how to scrape metrics from Kubernetes services) [learn more](https://prometheus-operator.dev/docs/operator/design/) resource that configures Prometheus scraping. The ServiceMonitor name typically includes the RouteMonitor name. It resides in the operator namespace (openshift-route-monitor-operator and has an owner reference back to the RouteMonitor, enabling cascading deletion.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.command: oc get servicemonitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator | grep console

common_errors.error: No resources found or grep returns no matches
common_errors.cause: ServiceMonitor not created yet, created with different name, or reconciliation failed
common_errors.solution: List all ServiceMonitors: oc get servicemonitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator. Check RouteMonitor status for error messages.

common_errors.error: Error from server (Forbidden): servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com is forbidden
common_errors.cause: Insufficient RBAC permissions to view ServiceMonitors
common_errors.solution: Request permissions or ask cluster admin to verify ServiceMonitor creation

steps.title: Inspect ServiceMonitor configuration
steps.learning_note:
ServiceMonitor spec defines how Prometheus (An open-source monitoring system with a time-series database that collects and stores metrics) [learn more](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/) scrapes metrics. The spec.selector field matches Services by labels. The spec.endpoints array specifies port, path, interval, and scrape timeout. The metadata.ownerReferences field links to the RouteMonitor, enabling Kubernetes to delete this ServiceMonitor if the RouteMonitor is deleted (cascading deletion).

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
 name: console-route-monitor
 namespace: openshift-route-monitor-operator
 ownerReferences:
 - apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1alpha1
 kind: RouteMonitor

steps.title: Inspect operator logs for activity
steps.learning_note:
Operator logs provide detailed insight into reconciliation logic. Look for log entries mentioning the RouteMonitor name (console-route-monitor). Successful reconciliation logs include 'Created ServiceMonitor' or 'Reconciliation complete'. Error logs indicate validation failures, permission issues, or API errors that prevent ServiceMonitor creation.

**Debugging tip:** Operator logs follow a pattern: watch events (resource created/updated/deleted), reconciliation start, validation, child resource creation, reconciliation success/failure. Understanding this pattern helps you quickly identify where reconciliation failed.

2026-02-18T10:30:15Z INFO controller.routemonitor Reconciling RouteMonitor {"name": "console-route-monitor", "namespace": "rhobs-test-routemonitor"}
2026-02-18T10:30:16Z INFO controller.routemonitor Created ServiceMonitor {"servicemonitor": "console-route-monitor"}

metadata.name: Cleanup RouteMonitor Test Resources
metadata.title: Clean up resources created by test_create_routemonitor_cr

system_impact.description: Deletes RouteMonitor CR and test namespace. ServiceMonitor automatically deleted via owner references. Prometheus stops scraping probe metrics.

safety.warning_message: This deletes test resources. Ensure you've completed all dependent tests first.

objectives: Understand Kubernetes cascading deletion and owner references
Learn proper resource cleanup procedures
Recognize the importance of namespace deletion for complete cleanup
Understand how operator finalizers affect deletion timing
Learn to verify cleanup completion

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Deleting namespace before verifying dependent tests completed
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Other tests fail because required RouteMonitor resources are gone
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always run cleanup tests LAST after all dependent tests pass. Check learning_path sequence.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not waiting for namespace deletion to complete
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Recreating namespace immediately fails with AlreadyExists error
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Wait for 'oc get namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor' to return NotFound before proceeding.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Assuming all resources deleted when namespace is deleted
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Verify ClusterRoleBindings and other cluster-scoped resources if test created any.

test_execution.objective: Safely delete all resources created during test_create_routemonitor_cr test, including RouteMonitor CR, test namespace, and verify cascading deletion of dependent resources like ServiceMonitor.
prerequisites: test_create_routemonitor_cr completed successfully
All tests dependent on RouteMonitor have finished (test_verify_probe_metrics, etc.)
Permissions to delete namespaces and RouteMonitors

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note: Before deletion, inventory what will be removed. This prevents accidental deletion of production resources and provides a checklist for verification after cleanup. Document resource names, namespaces, and dependencies.
steps.command: oc get routemonitor console-route-monitor -n rhobs-test-routemonitor && oc get servicemonitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator | grep console

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io "console-route-monitor" not found
common_errors.cause: Resource already deleted or test_create_routemonitor_cr was not run
common_errors.solution: Verify test was run: oc get routemonitors -A. If resources don't exist, cleanup already done.

steps.title: Inspect ServiceMonitor configuration
steps.learning_note:
Owner references create parent-child relationships between resources. When a parent (RouteMonitor is deleted, Kubernetes automatically deletes children (ServiceMonitor via garbage collection. The ownerReferences field in ServiceMonitor metadata should reference the RouteMonitor. This enables clean, atomic cleanup.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.command: oc get servicemonitor console-route-monitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator -o yaml | grep -A 10 ownerReferences
steps.expected_output:
ownerReferences:
- apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1alpha1
 blockOwnerDeletion: true
 controller: true
 kind: RouteMonitor
 name: console-route-monitor
 uid: <uid>

steps.title: Delete RouteMonitor custom resource
steps.learning_note: Deleting the RouteMonitor sends a DELETE request to the API server. If the resource has finalizers, it enters 'Terminating' state while finalizers run cleanup logic. Once finalizers complete, the resource is removed from etcd. Cascading deletion then removes owned resources (ServiceMonitor).

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io "console-route-monitor" not found
common_errors.cause: Resource already deleted
common_errors.solution: This is acceptable - cleanup is idempotent. Continue to next step.

steps.title: Identify target route to monitor
steps.learning_note:
Resources with finalizers may take seconds to minutes to delete while cleanup logic runs. The 'Terminating' state indicates deletion in progress. Wait for the resource to fully disappear before proceeding. If stuck in Terminating, check finalizers and operator logs.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output: Error from server (NotFound): routemonitors.monitoring.openshift.io "console-route-monitor" not found

common_errors.error: NAME shows but STATUS stuck in Terminating
common_errors.cause: Finalizer not completing or operator not processing deletion
common_errors.solution: Wait 60 seconds. If still stuck, check finalizers: oc get routemonitor console-route-monitor -n rhobs-test-routemonitor -o yaml | grep finalizers -A 5

steps.title: Verify ServiceMonitor creation
steps.learning_note:
Because ServiceMonitor has an owner reference to RouteMonitor, Kubernetes garbage collection automatically deletes it when the parent is deleted. This happens asynchronously - usually within 5-10 seconds. Verify by confirming ServiceMonitor no longer exists.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output: Error from server (NotFound): servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com "console-route-monitor" not found

common_errors.cause: Owner reference missing or blockOwnerDeletion=false, garbage collection disabled, or API server lag
common_errors.solution: Manually delete: oc delete servicemonitor console-route-monitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator

steps.title: Delete test namespace
steps.learning_note: Deleting a namespace deletes ALL resources within it. This is the most thorough cleanup method. Namespace deletion is asynchronous and can take 30-60 seconds as it finalizes all contained resources. Use this for complete test isolation cleanup.

common_errors.error: Error from server (Conflict): namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor is being deleted
common_errors.cause: Namespace already in deletion process
common_errors.solution: Wait for deletion to complete. Check status: oc get namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor

steps.title: Wait for namespace deletion to complete
steps.learning_note:
Namespace deletion triggers cleanup of all resources inside it. The namespace enters 'Terminating' state while this happens. It must fully disappear before you can recreate it. Stuck namespaces indicate resources with finalizers that aren't completing - check for PVCs, custom resources with finalizers, or API services that are down.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.expected_output: Error from server (NotFound): namespaces "rhobs-test-routemonitor" not found

common_errors.error: Namespace stuck in Terminating state for > 5 minutes
common_errors.cause: Resource with finalizer not completing, or API extension down
common_errors.solution: List resources in namespace: oc api-resources --verbs=list --namespaced -o name | xargs -n 1 oc get --show-kind --ignore-not-found -n rhobs-test-routemonitor. Manually remove finalizers if needed.

steps.title: Query probe success metrics
steps.learning_note: When ServiceMonitor is deleted, the Prometheus Operator removes corresponding scrape configuration from Prometheus. Prometheus stops scraping the probe metrics endpoint. This happens automatically via the operator's reconciliation loop. Verify by checking Prometheus targets or querying for the metrics (should return no results).
steps.command: oc exec -n openshift-monitoring Prometheus -k8s-0 -- promtool query instant 'http://localhost:9090' 'probe_success{job="console-route-monitor"}'
steps.expected_output: Error: no data points found (or empty result set)

common_errors.cause: Prometheus hasn't reloaded configuration yet, or metrics still in memory from last scrape
common_errors.solution: Wait 1-2 minutes for Prometheus config reload. Old metrics will age out after retention period.

steps.title: Verify Route Monitor Operator namespace exists
steps.learning_note:
Comprehensive post-cleanup verification ensures no orphaned resources remain. Check all namespaces where test resources could exist. Confirm RouteMonitors, ServiceMonitors, test namespaces, and any other test-created resources are gone. This prevents resource leaks and ensures clean test isolation.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.command: oc get routemonitors -A | grep console-route-monitor && oc get servicemonitors -A | grep console-route-monitor && oc get namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor
steps.expected_output: (all commands should return NotFound errors or no matches)

success_criteria: RouteMonitor console-route-monitor returns NotFound
ServiceMonitor console-route-monitor returns NotFound
Namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor returns NotFound
Prometheus no longer scraping console-route-monitor metrics
No orphaned resources remaining in cluster
validation.what_success_looks_like: All resources created during test_create_routemonitor_cr are deleted. Commands to retrieve them return NotFound errors. Namespace is fully removed (not stuck in Terminating). ServiceMonitor was automatically deleted via cascading deletion. Prometheus configuration updated to remove probe scraping.
validation.what_failure_looks_like: Resources still exist after deletion commands. Namespace stuck in Terminating state. ServiceMonitor not deleted (orphaned). Commands to retrieve resources succeed when they should fail with NotFound.

common_issues.symptoms: oc get namespace shows STATUS Terminating for > 5 minutes
possible_causes: Resource with finalizer not completing deletion
API extension service down (CRD's API group unavailable)
diagnostic_steps: List all resources in namespace: oc api-resources --verbs=list --namespaced -o name | xargs -n 1 oc get --show-kind --ignore-not-found -n rhobs-test-routemonitor
Check namespace status: oc get namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor -o yaml | grep -A 10 status
Look for finalizers: oc get all -n rhobs-test-routemonitor -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.finalizers'
Check API services: oc get apiservices | grep False
solutions: Remove finalizers from stuck resources: oc patch <resource> <name> -n rhobs-test-routemonitor -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge
Delete stuck resources individually: oc delete <resource> --grace-period=0 --force -n rhobs-test-routemonitor
Restart API extension if service down: oc delete pod -n <operator-namespace> <operator-pod>

As last resort, manually remove namespace finalizer: oc get namespace rhobs-test-routemonitor -o json | jq '.spec.finalizers = []' | oc replace --raw /api/v1/namespaces/rhobs-test-routemonitor/finalize -f -

common_issues.issue: ServiceMonitor not deleted via cascading deletion
common_issues.symptoms: RouteMonitor deleted but ServiceMonitor still exists
possible_causes: ServiceMonitor created manually without owner reference
diagnostic_steps: Check ServiceMonitor owner references: oc get servicemonitor console-route-monitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator -o yaml | grep -A 10 ownerReferences
Verify garbage collection enabled: oc get deployment kube-controller-manager -n kube-system -o yaml | grep enable-garbage-collector
solutions: Manually delete ServiceMonitor: oc delete servicemonitor console-route-monitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator
Wait longer - garbage collection may be delayed under load
Restart kube-controller-manager if garbage collection is malfunctioning

common_issues.issue: Cannot delete RouteMonitor - stuck in Terminating
common_issues.symptoms: RouteMonitor shows STATUS Terminating for > 2 minutes
possible_causes: Operator not running or not processing deletion hooks
diagnostic_steps: Check RouteMonitor finalizers: oc get routemonitor console-route-monitor -n rhobs-test-routemonitor -o yaml | grep finalizers -A 5
Check operator logs: oc logs deployment/route-monitor-operator -n openshift-route-monitor-operator --tail=100
Check validating webhooks: oc get validatingwebhookconfigurations
solutions: Remove finalizers: oc patch routemonitor console-route-monitor -n rhobs-test-routemonitor -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge
Restart operator: oc delete pod -l app=route-monitor-operator -n openshift-route-monitor-operator
Force delete: oc delete routemonitor console-route-monitor -n rhobs-test-routemonitor --grace-period=0 --force

immediate: Verify cluster is clean by listing all RouteMonitors: oc get routemonitors -A
Re-run test_create_routemonitor_cr if testing in a loop
Proceed to other test plans or test scenarios

system_impact.description: Read-only queries against Prometheus API. No modifications to cluster state.

objectives: Understand how blackbox-exporter generates probe metrics
Learn to query Prometheus using PromQL
Master interpretation of probe_success, probe_duration_seconds, and probe_http_status_code metrics
Understand metric labels and their role in filtering
Learn to access Prometheus via port-forward and API queries
skills_gained: Writing PromQL queries for probe metrics
Using kubectl/oc port-forward for service access

common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: No metrics found because Prometheus hasn't scraped yet (default 30s interval)
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Wait at least 60 seconds after ServiceMonitor creation before querying metrics

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not escaping curly braces in PromQL queries when using shell
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Shell interprets braces as brace expansion, query fails
Probe succeeds but application returns 500 errors - check probe_http_status_code
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always check both probe_success AND probe_http_status_code metrics

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not filtering metrics by job or instance label
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Query returns all probes, making results hard to interpret
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Use label filters: probe_success{job="console-route-monitor"} to scope to specific probe

test_execution.objective: Verify that Prometheus is successfully scraping probe metrics generated by blackbox-exporter for the RouteMonitor created in previous test. Confirm metrics show probe success, response time, and HTTP status code.
prerequisites: test_create_routemonitor_cr completed successfully
RouteMonitor and ServiceMonitor exist and are healthy
Prometheus Operator running in cluster
Access to query Prometheus (port-forward or route)
promtool installed (optional but recommended)

steps.title: Wait for operator reconciliation (The control loop process where a controller compares desired state (spec with actual state and takes actions to converge them
steps.learning_note: Prometheus scrapes metrics at intervals defined in ServiceMonitor (typically 30s). After ServiceMonitor creation, Prometheus reloads its configuration (takes ~30s), then performs first scrape. Wait at least 90 seconds total to ensure metrics are available. This prevents false negatives from querying too early.
steps.command: echo 'Waiting 90 seconds for Prometheus to scrape metrics...' && sleep 90
steps.expected_output:
Waiting 90 seconds for Prometheus to scrape metrics...
(90 second pause)

steps.title: Query probe success metrics
steps.learning_note: Port-forwarding creates a local tunnel to a Kubernetes service, enabling local access without exposing the service externally. The -n openshift-monitoring flag specifies the namespace. Port 9090 is Prometheus's default web UI and API port. The & runs it in background. Keep this running for subsequent query steps.

common_errors.error: Unable to listen on port 9090: Listeners failed to create with the following errors: [unable to create listener: Error listen tcp4 127.0.0.1:9090: bind: address already in use]
common_errors.cause: Port 9090 already in use by another process or previous port-forward
common_errors.solution: Kill existing process: lsof -ti:9090 | xargs kill -9, or use different local port: oc port-forward -n openshift-monitoring svc/prometheus-k8s 9091:9090

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): services "prometheus-k8s" not found
common_errors.cause: Prometheus not installed or deployed in different namespace
common_errors.solution: Find Prometheus service: oc get svc -A | grep prometheus

steps.title: Verify Prometheus API accessible
steps.learning_note: The /api/v1/query endpoint is Prometheus's instant query API. It evaluates PromQL (Prometheus Query Language - a functional query language for selecting and aggregating time-series data) [learn more](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/basics/) expressions at a single point in time. The up metric is a built-in metric showing scrape success (1 = success, 0 = failure). Testing with 'up' confirms Prometheus is responding before querying probe-specific metrics. The jq tool formats JSON for readability.

common_errors.error: curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 9090: Connection refused
common_errors.cause: Port-forward not running or not ready yet
common_errors.solution: Wait 5 seconds for port-forward to establish, then retry. Verify port-forward running: ps aux | grep port-forward

common_errors.cause: jq not installed
common_errors.solution: Install jq or omit | jq .status to see raw JSON output

steps.title: Query probe metrics from Prometheus
steps.learning_note: probe_success is a gauge metric exported by blackbox-exporter (A Prometheus exporter that performs HTTP, TCP, DNS, and ICMP probes and exposes their results as metrics) [learn more](https://github.com/prometheus/blackbox_exporter). Value 1 means probe succeeded (target responded), 0 means failed. The job label matches the ServiceMonitor name. The instance label shows the target URL being probed. This is the primary metric for alerting on probe failures.

common_errors.cause: No probe metrics found - ServiceMonitor not created, Prometheus not scraping, or probe failing
common_errors.solution: Verify ServiceMonitor exists: oc get servicemonitor -n openshift-route-monitor-operator. Check Prometheus targets: curl -s 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets' | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.job=="console-route-monitor")'

common_errors.cause: Probe failing - target unreachable, returning wrong status code, or timing out
common_errors.solution: Check probe_http_status_code metric for details. Verify target URL is accessible: curl -I <target-url>

steps.title: Query probe metrics from Prometheus
steps.learning_note: probe_http_status_code shows the HTTP response code from the probe (200, 404, 500, etc.). This differentiates between different failure modes: 404=not found, 500=server error, 0=couldn't connect. Combined with probe_success, this provides detailed probe health insight. Expected value is typically 200 (OK or 302 (redirect).

common_errors.cause: Probe couldn't establish connection - DNS failure, network unreachable, or SSL error
common_errors.solution: Check blackbox-exporter logs. Verify target URL resolves and is accessible from cluster

common_errors.cause: Target URL returns 404 Not Found - route exists but path doesn't
common_errors.solution: Verify target URL path in RouteMonitor spec. Test URL manually: curl <target-url>

common_errors.cause: Target service unavailable - pod not running, service misconfigured, or backend down
common_errors.solution: Check target service health: oc get pods -n openshift-console

steps.title: Query probe metrics from Prometheus
steps.learning_note: probe_duration_seconds measures total probe execution time in seconds, from initiating the HTTP request to receiving the complete response. This metric is critical for SLO tracking and performance monitoring. Values typically range from 0.05s (fast to 5s (slow). Values > 10s may indicate network issues or slow backends.

steps.title: Query probe metrics from Prometheus
steps.learning_note: Combining multiple metrics in one query provides comprehensive probe health status. This query returns probe success, HTTP status, and duration simultaneously. The regex operator =~ matches label values against patterns. This is useful for querying multiple probes or filtering by label patterns.

steps.title: Query probe success metrics
steps.learning_note: promtool is Prometheus's official CLI tool for query testing, rule validation, and metric debugging. The 'query instant' command executes PromQL against a Prometheus server. This provides cleaner output than curl and validates PromQL syntax. Install via: brew install prometheus (macOS or download from Prometheus releases.

common_errors.cause: promtool not installed
common_errors.solution: Install Prometheus tools: brew install prometheus (macOS) or apt-get install prometheus (Linux). Alternatively, skip this step and use curl queries.

common_errors.cause: Port-forward not running or wrong port
common_errors.solution: Verify port-forward active: ps aux | grep port-forward. Restart if needed.

steps.title: Check Prometheus target scrape health
steps.learning_note: Prometheus tracks scrape health for each target via the /api/v1/targets endpoint. The activeTargets array shows all currently scraped targets. The 'up' field indicates scrape success (up/down). The 'lastError' field shows the most recent scrape error if any. This helps diagnose why metrics might be missing or stale.

common_errors.cause: Prometheus can't scrape the target - endpoint unreachable, auth failure, or wrong port
common_errors.solution: Check lastError field for details: jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.job=="console-route-monitor") | .lastError'. Verify ServiceMonitor configuration.

common_errors.cause: ServiceMonitor not picked up by Prometheus or wrong label selector
common_errors.solution: Verify ServiceMonitor exists and has correct namespace selector. Check Prometheus ServiceMonitor RBAC permissions.

steps.title: Query probe success metrics
steps.learning_note: Cleaning up background port-forward processes prevents port conflicts in future tests. The pkill command sends SIGTERM to processes matching the name pattern. The -f flag matches against full command line. Verify it stopped with: ps aux | grep port-forward.

success_criteria: probe_success metric exists and equals 1
probe_http_status_code metric equals 200 (or expected status)
probe_duration_seconds metric exists and shows reasonable value (< 5s)
Prometheus targets endpoint shows console-route-monitor target as 'up'
Metrics have correct labels (job, instance, etc.)
validation.what_success_looks_like: All probe metrics are present in Prometheus. probe_success shows 1 (success), probe_http_status_code shows 200 (OK), probe_duration_seconds shows reasonable response time (<1s typically). Prometheus targets API shows the console-route-monitor scrape target as healthy. This confirms end-to-end monitoring is working: RouteMonitor → ServiceMonitor → Prometheus → blackbox-exporter → metrics.
validation.what_failure_looks_like: Metrics missing (empty query results), probe_success=0 (failures), probe_http_status_code shows errors (404, 500, 503), or Prometheus targets show 'down' health. These indicate broken monitoring: ServiceMonitor misconfigured, Prometheus not scraping, blackbox-exporter failing, or target unreachable.

common_issues.symptoms: Connection refused errors or port-forward exits unexpectedly
diagnostic_steps: Check Prometheus pod status: oc get pods -n openshift-monitoring | grep prometheus

Check network connectivity to cluster

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not obtaining fresh OIDC token before API request
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: 401 Unauthorized error due to expired token
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always obtain token immediately before API calls. Tokens typically expire after 5-60 minutes.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Using wrong tenant ID in API request
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: 403 Forbidden error or probe created in wrong tenant namespace
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Verify tenant ID with API administrator. Use dedicated test tenant for learning.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Creating probe with invalid URL (no scheme, invalid domain)
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Probe created in API but agent rejects it during URL validation
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always include scheme (https://), validate URL format, test URL accessibility first.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Expecting probe to be active immediately after creation
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Checking too soon shows status=pending, assuming failure
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Probe lifecycle takes 30-90 seconds: pending → agent validates URL → active → agent creates CR → running.

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not checking API response for probe ID
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Cannot query or delete probe later, orphaned resources
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always capture probe ID from API response: jq -r '.id' and store for cleanup.

test_execution.objective: Create a probe definition via RHOBS Synthetics API, verify the rhobs-synthetics-agent reconciles it into a Probe CR, and confirm blackbox-exporter executes the probe with metrics appearing in Prometheus.
prerequisites: Access to RHOBS Synthetics API endpoint (stage environment)
OIDC credentials for API authentication (client ID, client secret)
Tenant ID for test tenant
rhobs-synthetics-agent deployed and healthy in cluster
Permissions to view Probe CRs and blackbox-exporter resources
curl and jq installed

steps.title: Set API endpoint and tenant ID variables
steps.learning_note: RHOBS Synthetics API is deployed per environment (stage, production). The API endpoint URL varies by environment. Tenant ID identifies which namespace probes belong to for multi-tenancy (The ability to serve multiple customers (tenants) from a single instance while maintaining data isolation) [learn more](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/multi-tenancy/) isolation. Setting these as environment variables simplifies subsequent curl commands and makes the test portable across environments.
steps.command:
export RHOBS_API_URL='https://rhobs-synthetics-api-stage.apps.cluster.example.com'
export TENANT_ID='test-tenant-123'
echo "API URL: $RHOBS_API_URL"
echo "Tenant ID: $TENANT_ID"

steps.title: Obtain OIDC token for API authentication
steps.learning_note: RHOBS Synthetics API uses OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow for authentication. The token endpoint exchanges client ID and client secret for a JWT access token. The token includes tenant claims for authorization. Token lifetimes vary (typically 1 hour). The jq command extracts the access_token field from JSON response.
steps.command:
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'https://sso.redhat.com/auth/realms/rhobs/protocol/openid-connect/token' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
 -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
 -d 'client_id=rhobs-test-client' \
 -d 'client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET' \
 | jq -r '.access_token' echo "Token obtained: ${ACCESS_TOKEN:0:50}..."

common_errors.cause: Authentication failed - wrong client ID, invalid client secret, or client not authorized
common_errors.solution: Check API response without jq: curl -s -X POST ... (no jq). Look for error field. Verify credentials with API administrator.

common_errors.error: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
common_errors.cause: SSL certificate verification failing for SSO endpoint
common_errors.solution: Add -k flag to curl for testing (NOT for production). Or install CA certificate bundle.

steps.title: Obtain OIDC token for API authentication
steps.learning_note: The /api/v1/probes endpoint lists all probes for the authenticated tenant. This verifies: API is reachable, token is valid, tenant authorization works, and API is responding. The HTTP 200 status indicates success. Empty array [] is expected if no probes exist yet. This is a safe read-only validation before creating resources.

common_errors.cause: Token invalid, expired, or not included in request
common_errors.solution: Regenerate token (step 2). Verify Authorization header format: 'Bearer <token>' with space.

common_errors.cause: Token valid but tenant ID unauthorized or doesn't exist
common_errors.solution: Verify tenant ID with: echo $TENANT_ID. Contact API administrator to confirm tenant access.

common_errors.cause: Wrong API endpoint URL or API not deployed
common_errors.solution: Verify API URL: echo $RHOBS_API_URL. Check API route: oc get route -n rhobs-synthetics-api

common_errors.cause: DNS resolution failure or wrong hostname
common_errors.solution: Verify hostname resolves: nslookup <hostname>. Check API URL for typos.

steps.title: Create probe JSON payload
steps.learning_note: Probe definitions use JSON schema with required fields: url (target to probe), labels (key-value pairs for filtering/grouping), interval (how often to probe in seconds). Optional fields include timeout, expected_status_code, method (GET/POST/HEAD). The tenant field is set via X-Tenant-ID header, not in payload. Labels enable querying and filtering probes by environment, team, service, etc.

common_errors.error: jq parse error: Invalid numeric literal
common_errors.cause: JSON syntax error - missing quote, comma, or brace
common_errors.solution: Validate JSON: cat /tmp/probe-payload.json | jq . shows specific error line

steps.title: Obtain OIDC token for API authentication
steps.learning_note: POST to /api/v1/probes creates a new probe. The API validates the payload, assigns a unique probe ID (UUID), sets initial status to 'pending', and stores it in the database. The response includes the probe ID - critical for future operations (GET, DELETE, status updates). Save this ID for cleanup. The API returns HTTP 201 Created on success.
steps.command:
PROBE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w '\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}' -X POST "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/v1/probes" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
 -H "X-Tenant-ID: $TENANT_ID" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d @/tmp/probe-payload.json echo "$PROBE_RESPONSE" | grep -v HTTP_STATUS | jq .
HTTP_STATUS=$(echo "$PROBE_RESPONSE" | grep HTTP_STATUS | cut -d':' -f2 echo "HTTP Status: $HTTP_STATUS"
export PROBE_ID=$(echo "$PROBE_RESPONSE" | grep -v HTTP_STATUS | jq -r '.id' echo "Probe ID: $PROBE_ID"

common_errors.cause: Invalid request body - missing required field, wrong data type, or invalid URL format
common_errors.solution: Check API response for 'error' field describing validation failure. Common: url missing scheme, interval wrong format (use '30s' not 30), labels not object.

common_errors.cause: Probe with same URL and labels already exists (duplicate)
common_errors.solution: Change labels or URL to make probe unique, or delete existing probe first

common_errors.cause: API server error - database unavailable, internal error
common_errors.solution: Check API logs: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-api deployment/api --tail=50. Retry after a minute.

steps.title: Obtain OIDC token for API authentication
steps.learning_note: GET /api/v1/probes/{id} retrieves a single probe by ID. This confirms the probe was stored correctly. Check that status is 'pending' - the agent hasn't processed it yet. The created_at and updated_at timestamps should be recent (within last minute). This is the API's view of the probe; the agent's reconciliation happens asynchronously.

common_errors.cause: Probe ID not found - wrong tenant, probe deleted, or ID typo
common_errors.solution: Verify PROBE_ID: echo $PROBE_ID. List all probes: curl -s -X GET "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/v1/probes" ... | jq .

steps.title: Wait for operator reconciliation
steps.learning_note: The rhobs-synthetics-agent polls the API every 30-60 seconds for new/updated probes. When it discovers a probe with status=pending, it validates the URL via HTTP HEAD request. If valid, it updates status to 'active', creates a Probe CR in Kubernetes, and configures blackbox-exporter. The entire flow takes 1-2 minutes. Watch for status change from 'pending' to 'active' to 'running'.
steps.command:
echo 'Waiting 90 seconds for agent reconciliation...'
for i in {1..18}; do
 sleep 5
 STATUS=$(curl -s -X GET "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/v1/probes/$PROBE_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant-ID: $TENANT_ID" | jq -r '.status' echo "Attempt $i: Status = $STATUS"
 if [ "$STATUS" = "running" ]; then
 echo "Probe is running!"
 break
 fi
done
steps.expected_output:
Waiting 90 seconds for agent reconciliation...
Attempt 1: Status = pending
Attempt 2: Status = pending
Attempt 3: Status = active
Attempt 4: Status = active
Attempt 5: Status = running
Probe is running!

common_errors.cause: Agent not running, agent not configured to poll this API, or agent reconciliation failing
common_errors.solution: Check agent pod: oc get pods -n rhobs-synthetics-agent. Check agent logs: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-agent deployment/agent --tail=100 | grep <probe-id>

common_errors.cause: URL validation failed - URL unreachable, returns error, or invalid format
common_errors.solution: Check probe details for error message: curl ... /api/v1/probes/$PROBE_ID | jq .error. Test URL manually: curl -I <url>

steps.title: Verify Probe CR created in cluster
steps.learning_note:
The rhobs-synthetics-agent creates Probe Custom Resources in Kubernetes based on API probe definitions. The Probe CR name typically includes the probe ID or a hash. The spec contains target URL, interval, timeout. Labels from API probe are propagated. Finding this CR confirms agent successfully reconciled the API probe into cluster resources.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.

common_errors.error: No resources found or grep returns no matches
common_errors.cause: Agent hasn't created Probe CR yet, or created with different name
common_errors.solution: List all Probes: oc get probes -A. Check agent logs for creation events. Wait longer (agent may be slow).

common_errors.error: error: the server doesn't have a resource type "probes"
common_errors.cause: Probe CRD not installed - agent deployment incomplete
common_errors.solution: Install Probe CRD: oc get crd | grep probe. Reinstall agent if CRD missing.

steps.title: Inspect Probe CR details
steps.learning_note:
The Probe CR spec defines the blackbox-exporter check configuration. Key fields: target (URL), module (http_2xx, tcp_connect, etc.), interval, timeout. The status subresource shows probe execution health and last probe time. Labels include metadata from the API probe definition. Owner references link back to controlling resources if applicable.

**Production context:** In production environments, this check would be automated in CI/CD pipelines and monitored via alerts. If this resource is missing or unhealthy, downstream functionality silently breaks, making proactive monitoring essential.
steps.command: PROBE_CR_NAME=$(oc get probes -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.target | contains("console-openshift-console" | .metadata.name' | head -n1 oc get probe "$PROBE_CR_NAME" -n rhobs-synthetics-agent -o yaml
steps.expected_output:
apiVersion: monitoring.rhobs/v1alpha1
kind: Probe
metadata:
 name: probe-a7b8c9d0
 namespace: rhobs-synthetics-agent
 labels:
 environment: test
 service: openshift-console
 ...
spec:
 target: https://console-openshift-console.apps.cluster.example.com
 interval: 30s
 timeout: 10s
 module: http_2xx
...

steps.title: Wait for operator reconciliation
steps.learning_note: After Probe CR is created, blackbox-exporter begins executing probes and exposing metrics. Prometheus scrapes these metrics based on configuration. Query probe_success to verify end-to-end flow: API → agent → Probe CR → blackbox-exporter → metrics → Prometheus. Metrics may take 1-2 minutes to appear after Probe CR creation due to scrape intervals.
steps.command:
oc port-forward -n openshift-monitoring svc/prometheus-k8s 9090:9090 &
sleep 5
curl -s 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=probe_success{job=~".*console.*"}' | jq '.data.result[] | {metric: .metric.job, instance: .metric.instance, value: .value[1]}'
pkill -f 'port-forward.*prometheus'

common_errors.cause: Prometheus not scraping yet, metrics not exposed, or probe failing
common_errors.solution: Wait 60 seconds for scrape. Check Prometheus targets. Verify Probe CR status. Check blackbox-exporter logs.

steps.title: Obtain OIDC token for API authentication
steps.learning_note: Once the probe is executing successfully and metrics are flowing, the agent updates the probe status in the API to 'running'. This confirms the complete lifecycle: pending (created → active (validated → running (executing). The updated_at timestamp shows when the agent last modified the probe. This status update confirms bidirectional communication: API → agent (create and agent → API (status update).
steps.command:
curl -s -X GET "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/v1/probes/$PROBE_ID" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
 -H "X-Tenant-ID: $TENANT_ID" | jq '{id: .id, url: .url, status: .status, updated_at: .updated_at}'

common_errors.cause: Agent not updating status back to API, or probe execution failing
common_errors.solution: Check agent logs for status update errors. Verify agent has API write permissions. Check probe execution in blackbox-exporter.

success_criteria: Probe created in API with HTTP 201, probe ID returned
Probe status transitions: pending → active → running
Probe CR created in cluster by agent
Probe CR spec matches API probe definition (URL, labels, interval)
probe_success metric appears in Prometheus with value 1
API probe updated_at timestamp reflects agent reconciliation
validation.what_success_looks_like: The probe definition is created in the RHOBS Synthetics API with status=pending. The rhobs-synthetics-agent discovers it, validates the URL, creates a Probe CR in Kubernetes, and updates API status to active then running. Blackbox-exporter executes the probe, exports metrics. Prometheus scrapes metrics showing probe_success=1. This demonstrates complete end-to-end integration: API → agent → Kubernetes → blackbox-exporter → Prometheus.
validation.what_failure_looks_like: API returns errors (400, 403, 500), probe stuck in pending status, no Probe CR created, agent logs show reconciliation errors, probe status becomes 'failed', no metrics in Prometheus, or probe_success=0. These indicate broken integration points: authentication failure, agent misconfiguration, URL validation failure, or probe execution errors.

possible_causes: Token malformed or truncated during export
diagnostic_steps: Check token content: echo $ACCESS_TOKEN | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d | jq . (shows JWT claims)
Verify token not null: echo $ACCESS_TOKEN (should show long string, not empty)
Test authentication: curl -v ... (check Authorization header in request)
solutions: Regenerate token (step 2)
Verify Authorization header: 'Bearer <token>' with space between Bearer and token
Check token expiration: decode JWT and check 'exp' claim
Ensure client credentials are correct and client is active in SSO

common_issues.symptoms: Probe created but status never changes from pending after 5+ minutes
possible_causes: Agent not configured to poll this API endpoint
Agent polling interval very long (> 5 minutes)
diagnostic_steps: Check agent pod: oc get pods -n rhobs-synthetics-agent
Check agent logs: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-agent deployment/agent --tail=200
Verify agent API configuration: oc get deployment agent -n rhobs-synthetics-agent -o yaml | grep -i api
Check agent RBAC: oc get clusterrole,clusterrolebinding | grep synthetics-agent
solutions: Restart agent pod: oc delete pod -l app=rhobs-synthetics-agent -n rhobs-synthetics-agent
Verify agent API_ENDPOINT environment variable matches $RHOBS_API_URL
Check agent has permissions to create Probe CRs and update API probe status
Reduce agent polling interval if too long

common_issues.symptoms: Status moves from pending to failed instead of active
possible_causes: URL validation failed (agent HTTP HEAD request got error)
URL format invalid (missing scheme, invalid characters)
URL unreachable from agent pod network
diagnostic_steps: Get error details: curl -s "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/v1/probes/$PROBE_ID" ... | jq .error
Test URL from cluster: oc run curl-test --image=curlimages/curl --rm -it -- curl -I <url>
Check agent logs for validation errors: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-agent deployment/agent | grep <probe-id>
Verify URL format: must include scheme (https://) and valid domain
solutions: Fix URL format in probe payload (add https://, remove invalid chars)
Verify URL is accessible from cluster network
Check DNS resolution: oc run dns-test --image=busybox --rm -it -- nslookup <hostname>
Disable SSL verification in probe config if using self-signed certs (test only)

common_issues.issue: Probe CR not created despite status=active
common_issues.symptoms: API shows active but no Probe CR in cluster
possible_causes: Agent lacks permissions to create Probe CRs
Agent namespace incorrect or doesn't exist
diagnostic_steps: List all Probes: oc get probes -A
Check Probe CRD exists: oc get crd | grep probe
Check agent ClusterRole: oc describe clusterrole rhobs-synthetics-agent
Check agent logs for creation events: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-agent deployment/agent | grep -i 'create.*probe'
solutions: Verify Probe CRD installed: oc get crd probes.monitoring.rhobs
Check agent ServiceAccount has create permission on probes: oc auth can-i create probes --as=system:serviceaccount:rhobs-synthetics-agent:agent
Ensure target namespace exists: oc get namespace rhobs-synthetics-agent
Review agent source code or contact maintainer if bug suspected

common_issues.symptoms: Probe CR exists, status=running, but no probe_success metrics
possible_causes: ServiceMonitor or PodMonitor not configured correctly
diagnostic_steps: Check blackbox-exporter logs: oc logs -n rhobs-synthetics-agent deployment/blackbox-exporter
List Prometheus targets: curl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets' | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.job | contains("blackbox"))'
Check ServiceMonitor: oc get servicemonitor -A | grep blackbox
Query Prometheus for any blackbox metrics: curl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=up{job=~".*blackbox.*"}'
solutions: Verify blackbox-exporter pod running: oc get pods -n rhobs-synthetics-agent | grep blackbox
Check Prometheus scrape config includes blackbox-exporter
Restart blackbox-exporter: oc delete pod -l app=blackbox-exporter -n rhobs-synthetics-agent
Wait 2-3 minutes for Prometheus scrape cycle
